name: Cloudflare
scope_notes: Covers Cloudflare (API, Zero Trust Access, R2). All plans have API tokens and 18-month Audit Logs v2; Logpush beyond 18 months is Enterprise; Access service tokens need Cloudflare Zero Trust; R2 credentials need R2.

controls.name: Client IP Address Filtering
controls.what: Token only works from listed CIDRs (verify endpoint excepted).
controls.setting: API token > Client IP Address Filtering; condition.request.ip

controls.name: TTL (not_before / expires_on)
controls.what: Sets when a token starts and stops being valid.

controls.name: Token permissions and resources
controls.what: Limits a token to chosen permission groups, accounts, zones or R2 buckets.

controls.name: API Token Provisioning capability
controls.what: Only members with this capability or Super Administrator can create account tokens.

controls.name: Delete / roll API token
controls.what: Deleting or rolling invalidates the token secret.

controls.name: Remove member from account
controls.what: User tokens become inactive when the user is removed.

controls.name: Leaked token detection (GitHub Secret Scanning)
controls.what: Tokens leaked in public GitHub repos are auto-revoked; private-repo leaks only notify.

controls.name: Change Global API Key
controls.what: Replaces the user's Global API Key.
controls.setting: My Profile > API Tokens > API Keys > Change

controls.name: Change Origin CA key
controls.what: Immediately invalidates all previously shown Origin CA key values.
controls.setting: User Profile > API Tokens > API Keys > Origin CA Key > Change

controls.name: Service Token Duration
controls.what: Sets the service token's expiration date.
controls.setting: Zero Trust > Access controls > Service credentials > Service Tokens

controls.name: Automatically clean up inactive service tokens
controls.what: Disables or deletes tokens unused for 30-365 days.
controls.setting: Zero Trust > Access controls > Access settings > Manage service tokens

controls.name: Strict service token authentication
controls.what: Only Service Auth policies authorize token requests, no session cookie is issued, and failures are logged.
controls.setting: Zero Trust > Access controls > Access settings; strict_service_token_auth

controls.name: Disable / delete service token
controls.what: Disable stops authentication; delete revokes for good.
controls.setting: Service Tokens > Disable token / Delete; DELETE .../access/service_tokens/{id}

controls.name: Rotate service token secret
controls.what: Issues a new secret with an optional grace period for the old one.

controls.name: Enable API Access / API Access (member-level)
controls.what: Enterprise Super Administrators can turn off API access for the whole account or for specific members; member settings override the account setting.
controls.setting: Members page > Enable API Access; per member: API Access

no_control.what: No IP restriction or expiry for the Global API Key.
Global API Key cannot be limited to specific resources or permissions.
IP filter does not apply to the Verify Token endpoint.
Changing the Origin CA key is not recorded in Audit Logs.
Revoking existing Access sessions does not stop a valid service token; only deletion does.

controls_unknown: Any account-level setting to block members from creating user API tokens or using the Global API Key.
Any account-wide policy forcing token expiry or IP filters.
Whether Super Administrators can list or revoke other members' user API tokens.
Whether dashboard SSO or Access policies are checked on API token / Global API Key requests (no explicit statement).
Exact Audit Logs v2 action names for token create/delete/roll.
Whether Origin CA keys still authenticate after the 2026-09-30 removal date.
IP restrictions for Access service tokens and for R2 S3 requests.
Cloudflare OAuth tokens (actor context 'oauth', e.g. Wrangler) were not researched.

authentication.summary: Bearer token (cfut_ prefix) created under My Profile > API Tokens. Acts for one user with a subset of that user's permissions, scoped per account/zone/permission group.

federation.details: Dashboard SSO is a login control. Docs tell admins to keep an API token to disable SSO if the IdP locks them out, which implies tokens are not checked against the IdP; no doc states this outright.

ip_restriction.boundary: Per-token Client IP Address Filtering on API requests; off by default; not applied to the Verify Token endpoint.

lifetime.summary: Never expires by default; optional not_before/expires_on TTL

renewal.expiry_basis: Valid until deleted, rolled or TTL end
renewal.summary: Roll generates a new secret with the same permissions and invalidates the old one.

administration.summary: Any member can create tokens up to their own permissions. Tokens go inactive when the user is removed from the account. No documented account-level setting to block or approve user tokens.

offboard.details: User tokens inherit the user's permissions; docs warn a user token breaks when the user's policies are revoked. R2 docs say user tokens go inactive when the user is removed.

inventory.details: GET /user/tokens lists only tokens the caller created; admins see other users' token use only via audit log actor.token_id.

reads.ui: Manage Account > Audit Logs > remove the 'Action type is not view' filter (or set Action type = view)

offboard.ui: Manage Account > Members > expand member > Revoke > Yes, revoke access

token_format.notes: cfut_ + 40 chars + checksum; pre-2026 tokens are 40-char unprefixed.

log_sources.name: Audit Logs v2
log_sources.notes: All plans; 18 months; API GET /accounts/{account_id}/logs/audit; dashboard hides view actions by default and queries 90 days.

authentication.summary: Client ID + Client Secret (cfast_ prefix for new secrets) sent as CF-Access-Client-Id/CF-Access-Client-Secret headers to reach apps protected by Cloudflare Access.

federation.details: Service Auth policies authorize the token without an IdP login.

ip_restriction.boundary: Add an IP ranges Require rule to the Service Auth policy of each Access application; IP ranges are checked at login and continuously. Not a property of the token itself.

lifetime.summary: Duration chosen at creation; optional auto-disable/delete after 30-365 days of inactivity

renewal.expiry_basis: Duration from creation; Refresh adds one year
renewal.summary: Refresh or edit duration; rotate secret with a 1 hour to 30 day grace period.

administration.summary: Admins can disable, delete, rotate and auto-clean tokens; strict service token mode (forced on for orgs created on/after 2026-10-05) stops cookie issuance and logs failures.

sso.details: Service tokens are used with Service Auth policies, which do not require an IdP login.

offboard.details: Service tokens are account-level credentials for automated systems, not tied to a user.

credentials.name: R2 S3 API credentials (Access Key ID / Secret Access Key)

authentication.summary: S3 SigV4 credentials derived from a user or account API token: Access Key ID = token id, Secret = SHA-256 of token value. Temporary credentials can be minted from them.

federation.details: Same as the parent API token.

ip_restriction.boundary: Whether the parent token's IP filter applies to S3 requests is not stated.

lifetime.summary: Follows the parent token; account tokens valid until revoked or expiry

renewal.summary: Recreate or roll the parent token.

administration.summary: Permissions can be limited to object read/write on specific buckets. Revoking the parent token kills derived temporary credentials immediately.

offboard.details: R2 user API tokens go inactive when the user is removed from the account; account API tokens are not tied to a user.

inventory.details: R2 credentials are API tokens: account tokens are listable by Super Administrators (GET /accounts/{account_id}/tokens); user tokens only by their owner.

token_format.notes: Access Key ID is the parent API token id; secret is SHA-256 of token value.
